newsitem.title: USA: Maine Turnpike advisory group to recommend options.
newsitem.headline: Maine Turnpike advisory group to recommend options.

text.p: A group advising the Maine Turnpike Authority likely will recommend various options to combat traffic but failed to fully agree on whether to widen the road, an agency spokesman said Wednesday.

David Paradee said the Authority expects to get the report from the public advisory group on Thursday, the same date that a study by an independent consulting firm is due, but added that the agency will not make any decisions until after it has held public workshops.
"It could be well into next year before the Turnpike Authority decides how to act on the recommendations."
The public advisory group did agree on additional measures the agency already is considering, including more bus service and electronic toll collection, to prepare for an expected rise in traffic.

However, a complete consensus on whether it would be necessary to widen the Turnpike, a project that in the past has been estimated to cost around $100 million, was not reached. "There was not perfect consensus but fairly strong consensus for beginning the permitting process to widen," Paradee said, explaining this process can take several years.
The Authority's debt ceiling totals about $156 million, so any expansion project likely would require increasing this limit, he added.
